## 2026-11-02 (214): end-to-end audit of Maple model 111 -- the truth is between the blend and the single texture
**The material equation, solved against the reference:** the draw renders as `albedo x light`, with the blend `albedo = lerp(A 0.4924, B 0.2356, mask C 0.5017) = 0.364` (sRGB) and the light term `lerp(dark 0.109, light 1.185, lm 0.549) = 0.700`. Our measured ground was 0.0685 linear, and 0.364^2.2 x 0.700 = 0.073 -- the material math is self-consistent. Xenia's ground there is 0.0273, which implies an effective albedo of about **0.162** (sRGB), far below the blend's 0.364.
**The candidates:** 282 = 0.5017, 276 = 0.2186. 276 is the closest single texture to the implied value.
**Tested** with a new diagnostic switch `FM2_FORCE_ALBEDO=<id>` (applies one candidate as the draw's sole colour):
```
Maple default (blend)   ground ratio 2.51
FM2_FORCE_ALBEDO=0x114  ground ratio 0.19   (texture 276 alone: far too dark)
```
So the blend is ~2.5x too bright and texture 276 alone is ~5x too dark -- the reference sits **between the two**, which is the "partial decode" signature again and cannot be expressed as a choice among the draw's own candidates.
**Conclusion:** for this draw no combination of its own layers produces the reference brightness; the residual is in how the textures are decoded on the way into the material (the same per-texture decode asymmetry documented in 211-213). `FM2_FORCE_ALBEDO` stays as a diagnostic.
**Defaults restored** (Maple re-imported, remaster rebuilt). Acceptance 5.08 (mask), 5.23 anchored, 5.80 ground-only.

## 2026-11-02 (216): plan v4 S1+S2 -- raw upload + display-space product is far too dark
**Implemented (both opt-in):** importer `FM2_RAW_TEX=1` (every FM2 material uploaded with `colour_srgb=false`, i.e. raw) and engine `FH1_FM2_RAW_TEX=1` (the lightmap branch multiplies the raw albedo by the display-coded light term and converts to linear once, `col = (albedo_display * lg)^2.2`).
**Measured (dense ground-only, three control tracks):**
```
track           default   raw + display product
Road Atlanta     0.41       0.32
Silverstone      0.49       0.03
Maple Valley     2.24       0.08
```
Everything is now **far too dark** -- the raw albedo multiplied by the light term and raised to 2.2 lands at 0.03-0.08 of the reference. The engine's post (`FinalCombineBloomTonemap` port) already converts linear -> display with its own curves and black point, so feeding it a *display* value converted to linear double-applies the conversion.
**What that teaches:** the missing piece is not just "raw + real order"; it is the post's input convention (docs say Bevy-standard linear). Either (a) the material must keep display values and the post must be fed display for FM2, or (b) the game's own post curve expects linear values that already include the display-space multiply done *before* an sRGB encode -- which is what the existing `FH1_RM_FM2_GAMMA_LM=1` path approximates. S1/S2 as planned cannot work without deciding the post convention first.
**Defaults restored** (three tracks re-imported, remaster rebuilt). Both switches stay opt-in.
**Acceptance unchanged:** road mask 5.08; anchored 5.23; ground-only 5.80.

## 2026-11-02 (217): plan v4 falsified -- the two colour-space orders give the same result
**S1b test:** raw upload (`FM2_RAW_TEX=1`) with the material passing the display-coded product straight through (`FH1_FM2_RAW_TEX=2`, no `^(2.2)`), versus the default (sRGB-decoded textures, linear lighting, post re-encodes):
```
track           default   raw + display pass-through   raw + convert-to-linear
Road Atlanta     0.41            0.39                        0.32
Silverstone      0.49            0.49                        0.03
Maple Valley     2.24            2.24                        0.08
```
The display pass-through is **identical to the default** (within the run-to-run spread). So decoding to linear and lighting in linear (with the post re-encoding) is mathematically equivalent, for these materials, to staying in display space -- the two orders agree. The only variant that differs is "raw then convert", which double-converts and is far too dark.
**Conclusion: the colour space is NOT the residual.** Plan v4's premise (the pipeline order is wrong) is disproven by a controlled experiment. The remaining error must be in the *values* -- albedo choice and lightmap value per draw -- which is what the per-draw audit (214) and the layer/mask arithmetic (203) already showed: our blend 0.364 vs an implied 0.162, with no candidate combination in between.
**Defaults restored** (three tracks re-imported, remaster rebuilt). All v4 switches stay opt-in.
**Acceptance unchanged:** road mask 5.08; anchored 5.23; ground-only 5.80.

## 2026-11-02 (218): BC4 passes through byte-identical, BC1 does not -- the colour-texture path is unverified
**Test:** the same `texraw` byte comparison that proved BC4 exact (MODLOG 181) run for the colour formats, against the Tsukuba guest dumps (`data/work/texdump4`, 962 textures from the verified grid run):
```
BC3 (fmt 20) 512x512   0 disc textures in Maple's folder -- the atlas crops come from elsewhere
BC1 (fmt 18) 512x512   26 discs vs 34 dumps, best exact match 5.4 %
BC4 (fmt 59)           (earlier, Tsukuba) 100.00 % on one pair, correlation 1.0000
```
So for BC4 the guest bytes are exactly the disc bytes, while for BC1 **no** disc texture matches any guest dump even approximately. Two readings: (a) the game re-encodes/unpacks BC1 colour textures before upload (a load-time conversion that BC4 does not get), or (b) the 34 BC1 dumps simply are not the 26 discs (different textures), and the test is inconclusive.
**This matters because the road draws' colour layers are exactly these BC1/BC3 atlas crops** -- the one part of the texture path never verified against the guest memory, and the place all the per-draw brightness evidence points.
**Next step:** match a BC1 disc to a dump by content (`texmatch`, correlation) rather than by exact bytes; if a match is found, compare the values to learn the conversion; if none is found at all, the discs' colour textures are not what the GPU samples and the importer needs the game's own upload path.
**Defaults unchanged.** Acceptance 5.08 (mask), 5.23 anchored, 5.80 ground-only.

## 2026-11-02 (220): the road draw's own shader constants found -- the per-layer scale/offset the importer ignores
**The probe now prints the draw's constants** (`FM2_PROBE_AT` line). Maple model 111 (`b57319ed5f943822`):
```
c0 [1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00]   c1 [0.08 0.08 0.08 0.00]   c2 [0.05 0.05 0.05 1.00]
c3 [0.20 0.20 0.20 0.00]   c4 [0.60 0.60 0.60 1.00]   c5 [0.65 0.65 0.65 0.00]
c6 [0.50 0.50 0.50 1.00]   c7 [0.10 0.10 0.10 1.00]
```
and the pixel shader's disassembly uses them as per-layer **scale/offset** pairs, e.g.
```
mad r5.xyz_,  r7.zxyy, c4.zxyy, c3.zxyy    ; tex * 0.60 + 0.20
mad r6.xyz_,  r0.xyzz, c2.zxyy, c1.zxyy    ; tex * 0.05 + 0.08
mad r10.xyz_, r0.xyzz, c6.zxyy, c5.zxyy    ; tex * 0.50 + 0.65
```
**This is the information the importer never uses.** Our blend path takes the raw texture means (0.4924 / 0.2356 / mask 0.5017) and lerps them, yielding 0.364; the shader first transforms each sample (e.g. the 0.4924 layer becomes 0.4924*0.05+0.08 = 0.105, or *0.60+0.20 = 0.495 depending on which sample feeds which layer). That is exactly the kind of per-draw data that could produce the implied 0.162 -- and it is **game data**, not a fit.
**Next step:** trace model 111's shader dataflow (which sample feeds which layer of the final oC0) from its disassembly, then apply the same `tex*s + o` transforms in the importer's blend path for these draws, behind a switch, and measure.
**Defaults unchanged.** Acceptance 5.08 (mask), 5.23 anchored, 5.80 ground-only.

## 2026-11-02 (221): model 111's pixel shader traced -- the constants feed a blend/light/specular chain, not a plain mean
**Traced the 192-dword pixel shader** (data/work/maple111_shaders.txt):
```
 28  mad  r10 = sample0 * c6 (0.50) + c5 (0.65)      ; bright version of the first colour sample
 29  mad  r6  = sample0 * c2 (0.05) + c1 (0.08)      ; dark version of the same sample
 30  mad  r5  = sample7 * c4 (0.60) + c3 (0.20)      ; second colour sample
 35  add  r6  = r6 - r5                              ; difference for the blend
 36  add  r0  = r10 - r8                             ; r8 = mad_sat(r2.z, c109, c108): the distance blend from the VS position
 38  mad  r5  = r5 + r6 * r3.w                       ; blend by the normal term
 33  mad  r1  = (c185 - c184) * r0.w + c184          ; lerp(dark, light, lightmap value) -- the light term
 61  mad  r0  = r1 * r0 + r2                         ; light x albedo + the specular sum
 63  mad  oC0 = r0 * r8.x + c114                     ; final scale + fog
```
**What the constants mean:** c1/c2 = offset/scale for the *dark* form of the first colour sample, c3/c4 for the second, c5/c6 for its *bright* form, c7 for the specular scales, c8 for the exponent. All are per-draw game values the importer never reads (it uses the raw texture means and a mask lerp).
**Why I am not folding them into the importer's mean-based blend:** the final colour is not `albedo x light` but `(light x albedo + specular) x fog scale`, with the albedo itself a distance- and normal-weighted mix of two transformed samples. Reproducing that correctly is exactly the pixel-shader evaluation that `bake_blend` does -- and with the bake on, Maple measured **5.22** (too bright), i.e. our evaluation of that same shader disagrees with the draw's real constants. So the remaining unknown is inside the interpreter's inputs (which c-registers it feeds and how), not in a transform we can add to the importer.
**Conclusion:** the constants are located and their roles are known; feeding them correctly is the interpreter work already scoped (vertex-shader varyings + register mapping). Nothing changed.
**Defaults unchanged.** Acceptance 5.08 (mask), 5.23 anchored, 5.80 ground-only.

## 2026-11-02 (228): the error is in the scene, not the curve -- sweeps and separations
Four measurements, each on the frozen pixel sets, that narrow P0's finding to two independent scene errors.

**1. Tone-curve sweep (`data/work/p2_tsweep.py`, t = 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1):** no t fixes any track.
```
track          best t   bins at the best t      note
Tsukuba        0.50     1.6 / 1.0 / 0.8         mid perfect, shadows 1.6x bright, highlights 0.8
Silverstone    1.00     5.7 / 0.8 / 0.6         no t helps (error flat at 0.87); highlights 1.7x dark
Sunset         0.00     0.9 / 0.6 / 0.4         uniformly too dark at every t
Maple          0.75     1.3 / 0.9 / 0.2         highlights 5x too dark at the best t
```
Totals 2.72 / 2.60 / 2.54 / 2.64 / 3.10 -- the curve moves the total by 0.5 at most and never fixes the highlights. **The curve choice is a second-order term.** (It is also already the game's own: FH1's tonemap/LUT/vignette are off for FM2 tracks, `main.rs` 228-232.)

**2. Is the light term flat? No** (`data/work/p3_lm.py`, `FH1_RM_FM2_DBG=3` + `FH1_FM2_POST=0` paints `lerp(dark, light, lm)`):
```
track           our light term p10/p50/p90      contrast p90/p10
Silverstone     0.025 / 0.991 / 1.000                39.7
Sunset          0.030 / 0.591 / 0.604                20.4
Maple           0.023 / 0.352 / 0.552                23.8
Tsukuba         0.024 / 0.462 / 0.491                20.3
```
The lightmap term carries real contrast, but **the median road pixel is at 0.99 light on Silverstone**: ~90 % of the compared road is fully lit, i.e. our shadow *coverage* is small, which is the known "shadows weaker" item.

**3. The invented light floor is not the cause.** `FH1_RM_LM_LIGHT_FLOOR=0` on the frozen pixels: 2.74 -> 2.76, dark bins unchanged (Tsukuba 2.21 -> 2.31, Silverstone 3.64 -> 3.64). Closed.

**4. Post off (`FH1_FM2_POST=0`) -- the decisive split:**
```
track         with the game's combine     scene only (no curve)
Tsukuba       2.21 / 1.33 / 1.00          0.86 / 0.62 / 0.47   curve multiplies ~2.2-2.6x
Silverstone   3.64 / 0.62 / 0.46          3.03 / 0.53 / 0.40   curve multiplies ~1.2x
Maple         3.21 / 2.15 / 0.45          2.04 / 1.40 / 0.31
```
**Silverstone's error survives the curve almost unchanged: shadows 3x too bright and sunlit road 2.5x too dark in the scene itself.** Tsukuba's scene is instead uniformly ~2x too dark (the curve then over-brightens it).

**Conclusion:** the road is wrong in two independent ways -- **lit road too dark** and **shadowed road too bright / too little shadow area** -- and the tone curve is a downstream consequence (our dark scene makes it pick the brightening curve). The per-draw albedo question (STATUS 6.1) is only one of the two, and the shadow term is the other. P3 therefore has a defined starting point: bring the lit-road value and the shadow coverage to the game's numbers, then re-check that the blend lands mid-range.

**Not tested:** no rendered change this turn; all four measurements are A/B on unchanged defaults.

## 2026-11-02 (230): the oracle works -- the game's own shader vs our engine vs the reference
**Correction to MODLOG 229:** `FM2_PROBE_AT` was never broken. It prints `[fm2]   model N ... -> lit G: family X ... | full Y`, and my filter in the earlier runs simply missed the line. Model 111 at the Maple road point gives `family 0.180 | none 0.180 | BC4 0.180 | colours 0.179 | all 0.205 | word 0.180 | full 0.104` -- the five gamma choices agree, so the shader's value there is not a gamma question.

**Importer (committed):** `FM2_PROBE_TOL` (height tolerance, default 1.5 = unchanged) and a diagnostic that prints, per draw, how many triangles contain (x,z) and the nearest height difference; plus a pending-geometry bounding-box report. No behaviour change at the defaults.

**`data/work/p3_oracle.py`** runs the draw's own shader at the world points under real road pixels (`FM2_PROBE_LERP` supplies the track's own V2LightmapColor1/2, because the staging folder has no `fx_globals.json` yet), and compares with our material's painted product (`DBG=4`, POST=0) and the reference at the same pixels. Maple Valley, linear green:

| pixel | game shader | our engine | xenia | engine/shader | lm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 759,451 | 0.164 | 0.0070 | 0.0040 | 0.04 | 0.277 |
| 279,475 | 0.183 | 0.0529 | 0.0194 | 0.29 | 0.368 |
| 339,475 | 0.153 | 0.0497 | 0.0284 | 0.32 | 0.392 |
| 687,487 | 0.238 | 0.1470 | 0.0382 | 0.62 | 0.453 |
| 843,403 | 0.245 | 0.0578 | 0.0529 | 0.24 | 0.241 |
| 123,403 | 0.133 | 0.0452 | 0.2542 | 0.34 | 0.224 |

**Two readings, and one caveat that has to be stated:** our engine renders **0.04-0.62 of the value the game's own shader produces at the same road point** -- never above it. That is a fitting-free statement and it matches MODLOG 228-229 (lit road too dark). **Caveat:** the probe's number is *unshadowed* (neutral light x lightmap), while the reference pixel includes the game's cast-shadow term -- which is why the reference is often far below the shader value (0.004 against 0.164 at the first point). So the oracle bounds the problem from above but does not yet separate "our albedo/light is low" from "our shadow term is weak".

**Next:** add the shadow factor to the comparison (the shader applies `min(1-(1-ShadowColor)*S, lerp(dark, light, lm))`, and `TrackSettings` carries ShadowColor), then the residual is the albedo question and the per-stage attribution is complete.

## 2026-11-02 (233): plan v6 written (docs/DESIGN.md, local) -- per-bucket instead of single-cause
**Why a new plan:** v5 assumed the whole error was the per-draw material brightness and sequenced an emulator capture to recover it. The measurements in MODLOG 225-232 show at least **two independent causes on different tracks**:
- Maple Valley: road albedo **0.35** against the game's own shader, with tight quartiles (0.29-0.38) -- a real albedo (bake/constants) deficit.
- Silverstone: road albedo **0.82** (essentially right) yet its rendered road is 2.5x too dark, and the error **survives the tone curve** -- a light/shadow/display error.
A global knob moves one and breaks the other, which is what every earlier global attempt measured.

**What v6 keeps:** the metric of record (asphalt-anchored, neutral in both pictures, frozen pixels, binned by the reference's brightness; baseline 5.38 / 6.77), the frozen reference hashes, the 12/12 draw map, and the shader oracle.

**What v6 changes:**
- **W0** classify all twelve tracks (albedo ratio + does the error survive POST=0) into bucket A (albedo), B (light/display) or mixed. Gate: no track "unknown".
- **W1** bucket A, Maple first: fold the draw's own `c1..c7` into the bake, or restrict the per-texel bake to the named draw. Gate: Maple albedo >= 0.85 and its acceptance 2.15 -> <= 1.0, others unchanged.
- **W2** bucket B, Silverstone first: a new statistic, **shadow coverage** (implied shadow factor from `curve(oracle)` vs the reference), then fix coverage or depth. Gate: bright third 0.46 -> >= 0.80, dark third 3.64 -> <= 1.50.
- **W3** re-measure the blend input t only after W1/W2 (it is downstream, MODLOG 227/228).
- **W4** close the loop: acceptance or a per-track residual table with named causes; no fitted values adopted as game data.

**Non-goals / stop rules kept:** no per-track gains, no global knobs, no emulator on the critical path (the ViGEm pad is ready if a measurement needs it), two attempts per step then write up, and any change that does not move the frozen-pixel metric is reverted rather than left behind a switch.

**First check inside W0:** confirm the oracle's units on a draw whose value already matched Xenia (Sunset's road, 3/255 historically), because every W1/W2 number depends on it.

**Nothing implemented this turn:** the plan is a document; no code or data changed.

## 2026-11-02 (236): plan v6 W2.1/W2.3 -- coverage is the problem, and it is the near road
**New statistic** (`data/work/w2_shadow.py`): undo the tone curve on both displayed values and divide by the unshadowed material, giving a shadow-ish factor per road point:
`S_game = curve^-1(X) / O` (X = reference pixel, O = oracle) and `S_ours = curve^-1(A) / P` (A = our render, P = our `DBG=4` product). Coverage = share with S < 0.6; depth = median S among those.

**Silverstone, 40 points:**
```
                     coverage        depth      median S
game (dark curve)      35%            0.42        2.07
ours (dark curve)       2%            0.51        1.83
near rows (y>=540): game 91%   ours 0%      far rows: game 14%  ours 3%
```
**Coverage is the problem, not depth** -- where we do shadow, the depth matches (0.51 vs 0.42). And it is concentrated where it matters: **the road within a few metres of the car is shadowed 91 % of the time in the game and 0 % in ours.**

**Near-car values (linear green), nine points:**
```
game 0.0040-0.0080     ours 0.0160-0.0232     unshadowed oracle 0.057-0.082
```
So the near road is **3-5x too bright**, and our rendered value is *above our own unshadowed product* (`S_ours` 2-11): our pipeline **adds** light there instead of removing it. With Silverstone's sun at ~36 degrees (`ShadowLightDirection -0.95, -0.70, -0.05`, `ShadowColor 0.45`), the game's car casts a long shadow across exactly that strip; ours does not darken it.

**Levers tested and ruled out for this:**
- `FH1_RM_SHADOW_DIST=600`: coverage unchanged (2 %), depth only.
- `FH1_RM_LM_LIGHT_FLOOR=0`: near road went marginally **brighter**, not darker -- the invented floor is not the cause (third independent confirmation).
- Sun elevation is not the explanation: 36 degrees gives long shadows, and the engine already uses `ShadowLightDirection`.

**Working hypothesis for W2.3, from the game's own shader:** the road shader gates its additive sun/specular term on the lightmap (`step(lightmap > 0.45)`, STATUS 2026-10-19 end 7/12), so in shadowed regions the term is zero. If our material adds its sun/specular unconditionally, shadowed road is lifted exactly as measured (our near road is brighter than our own unshadowed product). That is a one-term difference and it is testable next.

**Gate W2 (bright 0.46 -> >= 0.80, dark 3.64 -> <= 1.50): NOT met** -- no change was adopted this turn; the mechanism is now named and bounded.

**Not tested:** the sun-term gating change itself (needs a material edit); whether our car's shadow reaches that strip at all.

## 2026-11-02 (237): W2.3 attempted -- the gate hypothesis is disproven by measurement, and the decal change is rejected
**The step the plan named** was to gate the road material's additive sun/specular term on the lightmap (`step(lightmap > c253.w)`), because our near road renders 3-5x brighter than the reference (MODLOG 236). Two measurements were taken before changing anything:

1. **`FH1_RM_FM2_SHADOW_DBG=1` paints the shadow visibility** (`sh^3` in red). At the nine near-road pixels: `sh` = **0.47-0.62**, i.e. our shadow map is not missing -- the car does shade that road.
2. **The lightmap gate is already open there**: the same debug paints the light term in green, and it reads ~1.0 (lit), so `step(lm > 0.45)` would be 1 in both engines.

Together these say the sun-gate change **cannot** darken the near road: the shadow exists and the gate is open. The 236 hypothesis is therefore disproven before any code was written -- the near-road gap is shadow *depth/surface identity*, not gating.

**A real game-data difference was found and tested instead:** the projected car-shadow decal. The game uses `DropShadowColor`, which is **0.00 on nine of twelve tracks** (Laguna 0.02, Suzuka 0.06, Sunset 0.07), while the engine built the decal from `ShadowColor` (0.34-0.50). Implemented (reading `DropShadowColor`, old behaviour kept behind `FH1_FM2_PROJ_SHADOW_COL=1`), and measured on the same build:
```
track          ShadowColor decal (old)     DropShadowColor decal (new)
Silverstone    3.64 / 0.62 / 0.46  err 0.85   3.81 / 0.62 / 0.45  err 0.87
Maple Valley   3.07 / 2.15 / 0.47  err 0.88   3.21 / 2.10 / 0.48  err 0.88
```
**Worse, not better. Rejected and reverted** (per the plan's stop rule); the release engine rebuilt and the baseline verified bit-for-bit: Silverstone **3.64 / 0.62 / 0.46**, and the tree is clean.

**Useful by-products:**
- The metric is **stable**: Silverstone now reproduces exactly across repeated runs (3.81 twice, 3.64 twice). The earlier 3.10 reading came from a different build and is withdrawn as not comparable.
- The reference's near-road darkness (0.004-0.008 against an unshadowed 0.057-0.082) is **deeper than the game's own shadow rule can produce** (`min(1-(1-ShadowColor)*S, lerp)` bottoms out at `ShadowColor` 0.45, a 55 % darkening, not 94 %). So those near pixels are probably not bare asphalt -- the car body or its black decal is in them. **The "91 % vs 0 %" coverage figure is therefore contaminated by surface identity** and must be re-measured on a region the car cannot occupy.

**Gate W2 (bright 0.46 -> >= 0.80, dark 3.64 -> <= 1.50): NOT met.** No change adopted.

**Next concrete step:** re-measure coverage on the *far* road only (where the car cannot be), which removes the contamination, and treat the near-car band as a separate question about the car's shadow rather than about the road material.

Any future claim of "the total improved by 0.3" is therefore not supportable; only per-track, same-build A/B comparisons are, which is how every change in this plan has been judged.

**Gate W2 (bright 0.46 -> >= 0.80, dark 3.64 -> <= 1.50): NOT met.** Far-road coverage remains 3 % against 14 %, and the only lever found so far is per-track, not global.

**Next step (concrete):** the direction finding says the sun's azimuth is track-dependent, so the faithful fix is to derive each track's light vector from its own data rather than flip it globally -- Silverstone's `ShadowLightDirection` is (-0.95, -0.70, -0.05) and the engine's convention for its sign is what needs checking against the game's own code path (`0x825220f0`, STATUS 2026-10-19). That is a data/code check, not a fit.

## 2026-11-02 (239): the sun-direction hypothesis checked against the game's own code -- no convention bug
**What was checked:** `0x825220f0` in `data/work/fm2_xex/text.asm` (FM2's `default.xex`, decompressed). The function compares the settings object's current `+0x550/+0x554/+0x558` against sentinels and, when they match, **copies the caller's vector into them** (`stfs f0, 0x550(r3)` and the next two). It is a one-shot setter for `ShadowLightDirection`; it says nothing about the sign convention, and the engine already reads the same three attributes per track:
`crates/fh1-engine/src/track.rs:178` reads `ShadowLightDirection x/y/z`, and `:219` builds the towards-sun vector as `[-x, -y, z]` (travel direction negated, engine z mirrored), documented since 2026-10-19.

**Therefore:** the per-track derivation the plan asked for is already in place and agrees with the game's data path, so there is nothing to correct. The `FH1_RM_FM2_SHADOW_DIR=fx` result from MODLOG 238 (Silverstone coverage 3 % -> 10 %) is a **global sign flip**, not a per-track derivation, and it demonstrably trades tracks (Nordschleife 0.54 -> 0.82). Rejected; the honest reading is that Silverstone's coverage gain there was coincidence rather than a convention error.

**Consequence for W2:** the remaining coverage gap (3 % vs 14 % on far road) is **not** a sun-direction bug. The candidates left are the caster set and what the game bakes statically into the lightmap; neither is a one-line change, and W2's gate stays unmet: bright 0.46 -> >= 0.80, dark 3.64 -> <= 1.50 **NOT met**.

**No code or data changed this entry.**

## 2026-11-02 (240): W1 tested on the six A-bucket tracks -- FAILS there too, and that closes W1
The A-bucket tracks (albedo low, scene bins already below 1) were the one place W1 could still pass. Applied `FM2_SHADER_ROAD=1` -- the importer's draw's-own-shader albedo -- to Tsukuba, Sunset, Mugello, Nordschleife, Suzuka and Road Atlanta, rebuilt the remaster tables, and measured:
```
track            default err      shader-albedo err
Tsukuba             0.40              0.40
Road Atlanta        0.38              0.90     <- much worse
Nordschleife        0.54              0.56
Mugello             0.17              0.44     <- much worse
Suzuka              0.33              0.41
Sunset              0.62              0.64
sum                 2.44              3.36     <- worse
```
**W1 fails on both buckets**: Maple (MODLOG 235, 2.15 -> 3.62) and the six A-bucket tracks (2.44 -> 3.36). Reverted: the six maps re-imported with defaults, remaster rebuilt, and the baseline re-verified on three of them (Tsukuba 0.38, Road Atlanta 0.36, Mugello 0.16 against 0.40 / 0.38 / 0.17 measured fresh).

**What this establishes, and it is the important part:** an albedo that is *closer to the game's own shader* (0.29 -> 0.65 on Maple, and the shader path on six more) makes the picture *further from the reference* every time it changes anything. The reference's road is therefore darker than `albedo x lightmap` everywhere -- so the dominant difference is downstream of the albedo, in the light/shadow/display path, not in the bake. That is consistent with W2 and with the tone-curve sweep (MODLOG 228), and it retires the "per-draw material brightness" theory that the last several weeks were built around.

**W1 status: closed (failed, both buckets, reverted).** The bake is not the lever.

**The localisation:** our pre-post road is at **0.40-0.87 of the reference on nine tracks** (too dark) and **1.30-2.87 on three** (Sebring, Maple, TT -- already too bright). Then the dark tone curve (t~0) brightens what is already present, which is why Tsukuba, Road Atlanta and Laguna end up *too bright* in the final image while their scene is *too dark*: the curve overshoots. ## 2026-11-02 (258): new goal G6 (visual parity with every 360-era game) set as priority 1, and a priority order added

**What changed:** `docs/GOALS.md` gained a **G6** section and a **Priority order** table; the README's goals table gained a new row and an `order` column. No code changed.

**The goal, as recorded:** reproduce each Xbox 360-era Forza game's own look closely enough that the project's own measurement cannot separate ours from the original at the same pose. Games in scope: **FM2, FM3, FM4, FH1, FH2 (360)**. FM1 is original-Xbox and out of scope.

**Why it can be first:** it is the only goal with a working instrument -- frozen reference pictures plus `acceptance.py`, which prints a verdict instead of asking anyone to look -- and it is the yardstick every other goal is judged against.

**Status recorded honestly:** FM2 currently reads **6.04 against the target of 2.0**, every track off (best New York 0.48, worst TT King Cobra 3.49). `STATUS.md` §5-§6 name every cause with numbers and list ~20 rejected hypotheses; §12 records that no change inside the plan has an evidence-backed mechanism. So G6 opens as `in progress` with **an open decision blocking it** (accept / labelled calibration / park), not as a task list. That is stated in the goal rather than left implicit.

**Three things the goal now pins down that were previously loose:**
1. **Parity means the gate:** per-game aggregate `sum |ln| <= 2.0` and every track `<= 0.10`, against reference sets **frozen before** the work.
2. **A fitted gain is a calibration, not parity** -- labelled in the UI and the code, and it does not satisfy the gate. This is the rule that keeps `STATUS.md` §12's third option from silently becoming a "done".
3. **Parity is judged on the Remaster renderer at shipped default/high quality**, not on a low-end tier, so G5 cannot accidentally "fail" G6.

**Interleave with G1, stated explicitly:** G6 cannot be reached without G1's look slot, because the profile is where each game's visual values are stored. So G6's first two steps **are** v7.1/v7.2, with v7.1 gated on acceptance reproducing 6.04 / 6.86 exactly. The priority table therefore puts G6 first and G1 second, and says they interleave rather than queue.

**Priority order as recorded:** 1 G6, 2 G1, 3 S6, 4 G2 + G5's storage half, 5 G3, 6 G4, 7 G5's performance half. Ids keep their numbers -- `G6` is a new id, not a renumber, and the table notes that ids are for citation only.

**Not tested / unknown:** nothing has been measured for G6. FM3, FM4, FH1 and FH2 (360) have **no frozen references and no acceptance run at all**, so four of the five games in scope begin by building the harness FM2 already has.

**Not changed:** no code, no data, no rendering. The README row is a claim about a plan, and it stays in the "goals" section that says none of it is implemented.

## 2026-11-02 (255): PI conversion fixed and applied -- `prev = 99` plus letter-only FM2 race badges

**Changed:** `crates/fh1setup/src/cars.rs` gained one shared conversion, `display_pi(bands, pi)`, replacing two identical copies (in `fm2_cars.rs` and `fm4.rs`), plus `class_shows_pi(letter)`; both importers now call them. `crates/fh1setup/src/fm2_cars.rs` writes **no `pi`** for FM2's `R4/R3/R2/R1` cars. `crates/fh1-engine/src/race/postrace.rs` leaves the PI number empty when it is 0, so the class letter still shows and no "0" is printed.

**Why:** nine in-game readings (MODLOG 249-254) showed the shipped conversion was one point low. The rule that reproduces all nine is `display = prev + floor(f * span) + 1` with `prev = 99` for the first class (the scale bottoms at 100), and FM2's race classes show the letter with no number.

**Tested how:** `cargo test -p fh1setup --bin fh1setup` -- three new unit tests in `cars.rs`: the nine in-game readings, a band-containment check, and the FM2 race-letter rule.

```
test cars::tests::display_pi_stays_inside_its_band ... ok
test cars::tests::race_classes_show_no_number_in_fm2 ... ok
test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed
```

| FM4 | 503 | 254 | 246 | 3 |

**FM2: 74 cars lose their PI number** (letter only) -- every `R4/R3/R2/R1` car.

**The five cars that move down, recorded because they are the only regression risk:** `MAZ_AxelaSport_05`, `NIS_Fairlady432Z_69`, `CHE_Spark_11`, `FOR_Ka_11`, `TOY_Aygo_11`. All are in the **first class at the very bottom of the scale** (`FOR_Ka_11` normalised PI 0.001174 gives 100 where the old code gave 101). No in-game reading exists that far down, so this direction is **not verified** -- the nine verified readings all sit at f ≥ 0.06 within their class. If the game's floor turns out to be 101 rather than 100, these five are where it would show.

**A boundary case the tests caught:** a car sitting exactly on a class's normalised maximum would compute one past the class max (`f = 1` gives `prev + span + 1`). The conversion now clamps to the class maximum, so a number can never leave its own class. No car in the three rosters sits exactly on a boundary except one FM3 car at a class minimum, so this only guards the edge.

**Not done:** no re-import was run, so no installed content changed -- existing installs keep their old numbers until the cars group is re-imported. **Not tested:** the results screen with an FM2 race car (the postrace change is compile-checked only, not seen on screen).

## 2026-11-02 (251): PI conversion settled -- seven in-game readings, all exact, one constant

**What arrived:** two more Xenia screenshots. **FM2 2004 Audi TT Coupe 3.2 quattro = D 364** and **FM3 2009 Citroen C4 VTS = F 174**.

**Why the Civic was never the counter-example that 250 thought:** the rule in 249 used `prev = 100` for the first class. Using `prev = 99` -- i.e. the display scale bottoms at **100**, and the first class starts one below it -- the Honda Civic VTi lands on **211**, exactly as the game shows. The Civic reading did not refute the rule; it corrected one constant, and 250 mistook a wrong constant for a wrong rule. The Audi TT (364) and C4 VTS (174) then confirmed the corrected constant in both directions.

**The rule:** `display = prev + floor(f * span) + 1`, where `prev` = the previous class's `MaxDisplayPerformanceIndex` (**99** for the first class), `span = class max - prev`, `f = (pi - class min) / (class max - class min)`. One constant for every game.

| car | game | stored PI | class | shipped (`fm4.rs`) | rule | in-game |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R34 V-Spec II | FM2 | 0.379494 | B | 583 | **584** | 584 |
| Honda Civic VTi | FM2 | 0.098145 | D | 211 | **211** | 211 |
| Audi TT 3.2 quattro | FM2 | 0.232810 | D | 364 | **364** | 364 |
| R34 V-Spec II | FM3 | 0.285084 | C | 400 | **401** | 401 |
| Scion xD | FM3 | 0.067670 | F | 174 | **175** | 175 |
| Citroen C4 VTS | FM3 | 0.066769 | F | 173 | **174** | 174 |
| R34 V-Spec II | FM4 | 0.420014 | A | 502 | **503** | 503 |

**Tested how:** `data/work/pi_check.py` (the table above is its output; 7 exact, 0 not), and a roster pass over FM2/FM3/FM4/FH2 checking every car's computed number against its stored class band.

**Roster result:** FM3 415 cars, FM4 503, FH2 216 -- **none** outside its stored class band, computed values starting at exactly 100 (which is what the bottom-of-scale-100 constant predicts). **FM2: 21 of 310 outside**, all race cars -- R4/R3/R2/R1 share one display range (999) and one normalised maximum (1.0), so their number is not derivable from PI at all. A property of FM2's data, not of the rule.

**Consequence for the shipped importer:** `crates/fh1setup/src/fm4.rs` `display_pi` (line 158) is one point low on four of the seven readings (583, 400, 173, 502) and correct on the other three by coincidence. Every imported FM3/FM4/FM6 car currently displays one PI point low unless it happens to sit in a band where the two agree. **Not applied** -- still the user's call.

**Decompilation question, third position:** back to **not needed for stock PI**, because a stored-value lookup reproduces seven of seven readings exactly. Still needed for upgraded cars (per-part PI contributions) and for FM2's race classes.

**Lesson:** 250 called the Civic a counter-example after one reading and reopened a question on it. One contradicted reading is not enough to abandon a rule either -- and the right move at the time was to test the constant, which cost two readings and settled it.

**No code or data changed this entry.**

## 2026-11-02 (250): five in-game PI readings -- the rule matches four, and "identified" was premature (`superseded by 251: the fifth reading corrected a constant, not the rule`)

**What arrived:** two more Xenia screenshots (FM2 buy-car and FM4 car-select) showing the 2002 Skyline GT-R V-Spec II. Both confirm the R34 fixture **first-hand**: **FM2 B 584** and **FM4 A 503**, joining the earlier FM3 **C 401**. So all three R34 values are now in-game readings, not wiki figures, and 249's core point stands: the wiki was right and the computation was wrong.

**But the screenshots each carried a second car in the bottom bar, and one of them breaks the rule from 249.**

| car | game | stored PI | class | shipped (`fm4.rs`) | 1-based | in-game | diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R34 V-Spec II | FM2 | 0.379494 | B | 583 | **584** | **584** | 0 |
| Honda Civic VTi | FM2 | 0.098145 | D | 211 | 212 | **211** | **+1** |
| R34 V-Spec II | FM3 | 0.285084 | C | 400 | **401** | **401** | 0 |
| Scion xD | FM3 | 0.067670 | F | 174 | **175** | **175** | 0 |
| R34 V-Spec II | FM4 | 0.420014 | A | 502 | **503** | **503** | 0 |
| VW Golf GTi Mk2 | FM4 | 0.194195 | E | 242 | 243 | 275 | −32 (**excluded**) |

**The Golf is excluded, not a counterexample:** its bar reads `LVL2` on a profile showing 999,999,999 CR, so it is an upgraded car and 275 is its tuned PI, not its stock one. Recorded because a bottom-bar reading is only usable when the car is stock — that is a trap worth naming.

**So 249's "the conversion rule is now identified" is withdrawn.** The rule reproduces **4 of the 5 stock readings**; the fifth is exactly one high. Tested how: `data/work/pi_check.py`, output above.

**Two explanations, neither established:**
1. **The stored normalised PI is not the display source.** It is continuous — only 1 car of FM3's 415 lands within 1e-6 of a band integer — so if it were the source, a deterministic rounding would match every car. It doesn't, which points to the displayed PI being computed from car stats at load, with `Data_Car.PerformanceIndex` an approximation good to about ±1.
2. **FM2's first class starts at 99, not 100.** A base of 99 fits both FM2 readings; FM3 needs 100 (the Scion is 175 only with base 100). Two games differing in base is possible and unexplained.

**What would settle it:** one more stock reading in FM2's D class, and one more in FM3's F class. Scattered error in both directions inside a class = quantisation, so ±1 is the ceiling. Error only in the first class of one game = a base difference.

**Consequence, and it reverses something from earlier:** exact parity with the game's displayed PI is **not** reachable by converting `Data_Car.PerformanceIndex`. The best that gives is ±1. Exactness would need the game's own PI computation from stats — the decompilation work that 249 said was no longer needed. That is reopened in `docs/GOALS.md` S6 rather than quietly left as a win.

**Nothing applied to the code.** The shipped `display_pi` is one low on three of the five readings; the 1-based rule fixes those and breaks the Civic by one. With the evidence available, changing it would trade one error for another, so `crates/fh1setup/src/fm4.rs` is untouched.

**Lesson, and it is the fourth swing on one number:** four matches is not a rule. 247 blamed a memory, 248 blamed a wiki, 249 declared success on the matches and ignored that the sample was chosen by the same person who wanted it to work. The next reading contradicted it. Record the contradicting measurement before the conclusion, not after it is contradicted.

**No code or data changed this entry.**

**What changed:** a screenshot of FM3 running in Xenia (2026-11-02) settles it. The car select screen reads **2002 Nissan Skyline GT-R V-Spec II, C 401**. The bottom bar of the same screen also reads **Scion xD, F 175** -- a second in-game value, free.

**The rule, identified:** with `prev` = the previous class's `MaxDisplayPerformanceIndex` (100 for the first class), `span = class max - prev`, `f = (pi - class min) / (class max - class min)`:

## 2026-11-02 (248): CORRECTION -- the R34 comparison values are wiki figures, not game readings (`superseded by 249: the 401 was right`)

**What was wrong in 247:** that entry recorded "the user's value" for the R34 GT-R as 584 / 401 / 503 and treated the FM3 difference as an unexplained defect ("computes 400 where the user reports 401"). Those three numbers **came from a wiki, not from the game running or from its files** (user, 2026-11-02). So they were never evidence about the game, and a wiki disagreeing with the game's own data is not a defect in our computation.

**Retracted:** the "FM3 is 1 point low, cause unidentified" finding. There is no measured discrepancy. The game's own data gives **400**; the wiki says **401**; nothing has been read off the game's screen.

**What this does to the off-by-one claim in 247:** it previously rested on "two of three fixture values match the inclusive reading". That support is weaker than it looked, because the numbers are second-hand. It now rests on a structural argument from the data alone: under the exclusive reading two classes share a boundary number -- a car exactly at F's stored maximum displays **200 as class F**, while the next car up also rounds to 200 and is class **E**. A display number cannot belong to two classes, so the exclusive reading in `crates/fh1setup/src/fm4.rs` `display_pi` (line 158) is wrong regardless of what any wiki says. **The proposed fix stands; it is still not applied.**

| reading | FM2 R34 | FM4 R34 | boundary collision? |
|---|---|---|---|
| exclusive (shipped) | 583 | 502 | yes -- 200 is both F and E in FM3/FM4 |
| inclusive (proposed) | 584 | 503 | no |

**Also worth stating plainly:** if the parity target is a wiki table, the target is not game data, which contradicts the provenance rule this project runs on. The target is the number the game itself would display, and that is what the computation above produces.

**What is unaffected:** PI is stored (`Data_Car.PerformanceIndex`) and the ladders are stored (`CarClasses`) -- that came from reading the files. The ladders per game, the "74 of 310 FM2 cars' class is not derivable from PI", the part-separation result, and the 93.3-96.3 % rank agreement all stand.

**Still to do:** confirm at least one R34 PI **in-game** before the fixture is frozen, and prefer game-readings over wiki tables for every future parity target.

## 2026-11-02 (247): the goals plan worked through -- PI is stored data, models keep their parts, one backend number cannot be exact

**What changed:** `docs/GOALS.md` (local) gained a measured "what the files say" section under S6, an answered Q1, a partly resolved C5, and a rewritten "game data" table; new `docs/ATTACHMENT.md` (local) is the G4.1 attachment-point note. **No code, no data, no shader change.** The engine's rendering and the committed tree are untouched; nothing was written to any game install.

**Step 0 (writing the goals down) was MODLOG 246.** This entry is steps 1-4 of the plan agreed directly after it.

### Step 1 -- do imported models keep their parts separate? (conflict C5, which blocked G4)

**Tested how:** read the node list out of an actual imported car, `data/installations/.../cars/ALF_8C_08/model.gltf` (50 nodes), and the exporter that writes it (`crates/fh1setup/src/model.rs:151` writes one glTF node per carbin section, named as the game names it).

**Result: yes, fully separate.** `body, hooda, bumperFa, bumperRa, skirtLa, skirtRa, trunk, undercarriagea, glassF/R/LF/RF/LHL/RHL/LTL/RTL, mirrorL/R, headlightL/R, taillightL/R, interior, seatL, seatR, steering_wheel, wheel_LF..RR, caliper_LF..RR, rotor_LF..RR, exhaustRa`. So seats, steering wheel, calipers, rotors and lamps are already individual objects -- G4's interior and brake wishes are not blocked by the model format, which was the risk.

**Not tested:** the part-name inventories of FM2, FM3, FM4, FM5, FM6 and FH2. Their importers also emit one node per part (`fm2_cars.rs` uses the game's own part name; `fm6.rs` uses `<stem>_<material>`), but the names have not been read, so the mapping table in `docs/ATTACHMENT.md` marks those columns as blanks rather than as "the same".

### Step 2 -- is car PI stored or computed? (Q1, which blocked S6)

**Tested how:** `python -I data/work/pi_probe.py` and `python -I data/work/pi_bands.py`, read-only against `media/db/gamedb.slt` in the already-extracted FM2, FM3, FM4 and FH2 (360) discs.

**Result: stored.** Every game keeps `Data_Car.PerformanceIndex` (normalised 0..1, non-null on every row) and the ladder in `CarClasses` (`MaxPerformanceIndex`, `MaxDisplayPerformanceIndex`, class letter). Non-null counts: FM2 310 cars, FM3 415, FM4 503, FH2 216. The displayed number is a piecewise-linear interpolation of the normalised value between consecutive class maxima.

**The ladders are different in every game** (FM2 `D/C/B/A/S/U/R4-R1` at 400/550/700/850/998/999; FM3 `F..U` at 200..999 in 75-100 steps; FM4 the same but R2 at 875; FH2 `D/C/B/A/S1/S2/X` at 500..999), which supports giving the ladder to G1's menu-UI slot rather than computing it.

### Step 2b -- the fixture, and a candidate off-by-one in the shipped importer

The stored values, and the display conversion done two ways:

| car | game | normalised PI | stored class | exclusive | **inclusive** | user's value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NIS_SkylineGTRVSpecII_02` | FM2 | 0.379494 | B | 583 | **584** | 584 |
| `NIS_SkylineGTRVSpecII_02` | FM3 | 0.285084 | C | 400 | **400** | 401 |
| `NIS_SkylineGTRVSpecII_02` | FM4 | 0.420014 | A | 502 | **503** | 503 |

"Inclusive" = each class starts at the previous class's maximum + 1, because the stored maxima are inclusive last values (B is 551..700). It matches two of the three values; the current `crates/fh1setup/src/fm4.rs` `display_pi` (line 158) uses the exclusive reading and is one point low, which is what imported FM4 cars ship with today. **Recorded as a proposed fix, not applied** -- a code change is outside this investigation and needs the user's go-ahead.

FM3 computes 400 where the user reports 401; 400.08 (exclusive) and 400.42 (inclusive) both round to 400, so no convention choice explains it. Cause unidentified, recorded as unknown rather than rounded away.

**One more finding from the roster:** FM2's race classes R4-R1 all store `MaxPerformanceIndex` 1.0 and display max 999, so their PI cannot distinguish them -- **74 of 310 FM2 cars** have a stored class not derivable from their PI. The letter must be read from `ClassID`, never computed from the number.

### Step 4 (first pass) -- can one backend number reproduce every game? (Q2)

**Tested how:** `python -I data/work/pi_rank.py`, using each game's own normalised PI as a stand-in for "performance" and counting car pairs the two games order differently. This is a proxy for the not-yet-built backend rating, and is labelled as such.

**Result: no, not exactly.** Rank agreement between games is only **93.3 %-96.3 %** (FM2/FM3 95.5 % of 29,157 pairs; FM2/FM4 94.5 %; FM2/FH2 93.3 %; FM3/FM4 95.9 %; FM3/FH2 93.9 %; FM4/FH2 96.3 %). Worst single cars move 30-60 places (`DOD_ChallengerHemi_70` is #132 of 315 in FM3 and #72 in FM4). So some cars will be off by a class however the number is fitted -- now a measured size, not a worry. Caveat recorded: each game's PI carries tier effects, so part of the disagreement is policy, which argues for rating performance separately from tier.

### Step 3 -- the attachment schema

`docs/ATTACHMENT.md`: canonical point names mapped to the verified FH1 node names, frames expressed in **normalised car space** (wheelbase units, not metres) so a cross-generation kit can be fitted by a single uniform scale plus a yaw rotation, what the importer must guarantee (never weld parts, export the frames, declare the source), and the validation gate for cross-model cases.

**Not tested:** the normalised-space convention has not been tried on a real pair of models (e.g. an FM2 FD RX7 kit onto a later FD RX7). Until it is, the note is a design, not a schema.

**Next:** dump the part names of one car from each other game (unblocks G4), and decide whether to apply the `display_pi` off-by-one fix.

## 2026-11-02 (246): long-term goals written down (G1-G5) and a tracked summary in the README

**What changed:** a new local working document, `docs/GOALS.md` (git-ignored with the rest of `docs/`), holding the five long-term goals agreed in conversation on this date; and a short **Goals** table in `README.md` (tracked) listing `G1`-`G5` with a one-line description each, stating plainly that **none of them is implemented**. No code, data, shader or engine change.

**Why:** the goals existed only in the conversation, which loses them. A goal needs an id so work and MODLOG entries can cite it, a status, and above all a **gate** -- a measurable way to know it is met -- otherwise it degrades into "does it look right to me", which is the failure mode `STATUS.md` §3 records (a ten-week effort judged against a number that moved 3.3x when a threshold was nudged).

**The five goals, as recorded:**
- **G1 modular game features** -- every game-specific system as a named slot with a per-game provider, on two independent axes (look/behaviour, and quality tier). Includes the sixteen `if track.id.starts_with("fm2/")` blocks from MODLOG 245 as the look slot's first provider.
- **G2 complete car and track list** -- three stages (360+FM1; Xbox One era; PC/Xbox Series era), all layouts and test tracks, Horizon open worlds excluded except FH1 and FH2, an optional era year cutoff stored as a preset with a documented exception list, and non-destructive roster trimming.
- **G3 best model per car** -- behind a switch, every rendition of every car retained, all LODs kept, scored on two measurable axes (fidelity and part-separability) with recorded overrides.
- **G4 enhanced customisation** -- body kits, wheels, interiors, exhausts, lighting, stance, engine swaps, era-correct aero; blocked on a named attachment-point schema and on whether imported models keep their parts separate.
- **G5 optimisation** -- 720p60 on Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 class handhelds with a fixed named scene, plus "as small as possible" storage with a size report as the substitute gate (no numeric target by the user's decision).

**Also recorded in the document:** cross-cutting `S6` (one backend PI rating, measured on a frozen benchmark with a *fixed* rating physics, translated per game by a map fitted to that game's own roster; the R34 values as a named regression fixture) and `S7` (catalogue with provenance, measurable gate per goal, car browser dev scene, reproducible incremental import, save versioning); six conflicts `C1`-`C6`, of which **C5 is open and blocking** (if imported models are welded blobs, G4 needs a content-pipeline rebuild before any more cars are imported); eleven open questions `Q1`-`Q11`; and a table of values to read from the game's files rather than from memory.

**Provenance rule carried forward from plan v7 (MODLOG 245), with one documented exception:** every value that decides how something looks or behaves must be either read from that game's files or measured against a reference with a MODLOG entry naming it. Engine codes (`2JZ-GTE - 1998 Toyota Supra RZ`) are the exception, since the games' data does not contain them; the external source is recorded per engine.

**Deliberately not resolved:** the six conflicts are written down rather than silently settled, and `Q1` (is PI stored data or computed at load?) is named as the first thing that decides how good `S6`'s per-game maps can be. The next planned step is to read the game files for `Q1` and for `C5` (model part separation), both read-only.

**Not tested:** nothing here is a rendering or gameplay claim; no implementation exists, so nothing was run. The README table asserts no working feature.

## 2026-11-02 (245): goal restated and plan v7 written -- FM2 parity first, results stored as per-game visual profiles
**The user's goal (2026-11-02):** *first* visual parity with FM2; *and* the findings must make the other Xbox 360 Forzas cheaper; ideally a switch between each game's visual style. That reframes FM2 parity from "one finished thing" into "the first filled-in profile".

**What the code shows today:** the FM2 style already exists as a chain of **sixteen `if track.id.starts_with("fm2/")` blocks** in `crates/fh1-engine/src/main.rs` (146-420), each setting an environment variable (grade/LUT/vignette off, tone curve, shadow rule, specular, sky gain, camera, crowds, car knobs, exposure). It works, but it is a string-prefix test that no second game can join, the values cannot be listed or compared, and **inferred fits are indistinguishable from values read out of the game's files** -- which is how a project grows knobs nobody can defend.

**Plan v7 (docs/DESIGN.md):**
- **v7.1** move the sixteen blocks into `VisualStyle::fm2()` with **no behaviour change** (gate: acceptance reproduces 6.04 / 6.86 exactly; existing overrides still win);
- **v7.2** the switch `FH1_VISUAL_STYLE=<game>`, default = the track's own game (gate: forcing a style on a foreign track behaves as the override says);
- **v7.3** the remaining v6 parity work is expressed as profile fields, so each change is one named value;
- **v7.4** FM4 as the first other game (it shares the most with FM2), gated on it reporting its own acceptance table.
**Guardrail that gives the plan its value:** every profile field must be either *read* from that game's files or *measured* against the reference pictures with a MODLOG entry naming it. There is no third category, so an unsourced value gets no field.

**Nothing implemented yet:** the document only. The sixteen-block move (v7.1) is a refactor of `main.rs`, so it will be done as one isolated step with the exact-reproduction gate, not folded into other work.

| mean abs error from 1.0 | 0.150 | **0.137** |
| Silverstone | 1.07 | **1.00** |

improves two tracks clearly (Silverstone -0.07, Mugello -0.14), and moves two by +0.03 (inside the harness's noise).
